title: prefill-and-decoding-bandwidth-sku-delta-study
summary: Controlled study measuring how prefill and decoding phases expose different bandwidth and latency bottlenecks across A100, H100, and L40S SKUs and driver/CUDA combinations.
content:
Purpose: isolate prefill (large host->device transfers and KV build) and decode (many small autoregressive steps) to compare how SKUs and CUDA stacks shift bottlenecks.

Experiment matrix: M7B/M13B/M70B proxies; SKUs: AWS p4d/p4de, GCP A100/H100, Azure L40S_v2; CUDA stacks: 11.8+515, 12.1+535, 12.2+545. Workloads include prefill-heavy (8k prefill, 32 decode), decode-heavy (512 prefill, 1024 decode), and microburst small-token traffic.

Infrastructure and measurement: rw-runtime-serve:v0.12.2-perf with NVTX ranges around memcpy, kv build, kernel launches. Allocation policies compared: pre-allocate KV vs dynamic slab growth. Each test uses 20 warmups and 600 measured iterations.

Key findings: 1) Prefill throughput is primarily host->device bandwidth bound; NVLink-enabled A100 setups outperformed L40S single-card prefill by ~1.8-1.9x for 8k transfers. 2) Per-token decode latency favors H100 on our kernels; p50 decode on H100 ~10-15% faster than A100 given modern CUDA 12.x stacks, though p99 depends heavily on allocator contention. 3) CUDA/driver upgrades (12.2+driver 545) smoothed memcpy variance and reduced small-kernel launch costs when paired with updated kernels. 4) Pre-allocating KV cache significantly reduces p99 decode tail on A100/H100; benefit smaller on L40S due to memory bandwidth limits. 5) L40S showed larger tail amplification under microbursts; enabling stream pooling reduced tail by ~18%.

Representative numbers (M13B, fp16, batch=1): Prefill-heavy end-to-end p50: p4de(A100 80GB) ~1.8s, L40S_v2 ~2.6s, H100 ~1.6s. Decode-heavy per-token p50: p4de ~12.4ms, L40S ~14.9ms, H100 ~10.6ms.

Practical recommendations: route long-context prefill jobs to NVLink-rich SKUs, pre-allocate KV caches for high-QPS decode workloads, tune slab allocators if memory constrained, and schedule driver rollouts with smoke tests for memcpy variance and small-step decode p99.

Open follow-ups: add 32k KV experiments, test INT4 transfer impact, and replay real client traces for microburst validation.

Repro runbook: branch perf/sku-prefill-decode-2025 commit a7d9f1c; docker image rw-runtime-serve:v0.12.2-perf; bench driver command: bin/bench_driver --model m13b --prefill 8192 --decode 32 --batch 1 --iters 600 --warmup 20 --trace nvtx; env var ALLOC_POLICY=preallocate or auto.

Contributors: Maya Chen (lead), Samir Patel, Lena Rodriguez, Ethan Wu.

Status: in_review.
